meta.topic_note: Both papers touch on how evaluation data can leak into training.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.one_liner: The Transformer replaces recurrence with attention.

papers.title: A Study of Data Leakage
papers.one_liner: A controlled study of leakage in benchmark splits.

summary: The first paper introduces the Transformer, while the second studies how benchmark leakage can inflate reported results.

big_picture.explanation: The Transformer processes all tokens in parallel instead of one at a time.
big_picture.analogy: It is like reading a whole page at once instead of moving a finger along each word.
big_picture.why_it_matters: Parallel processing made large language models practical to train.

steps.title: Embed the tokens
steps.explanation: Tokens are mapped to vectors and combined with positional information.

steps.title: Apply attention
steps.explanation: Each position attends to every other position in the sequence.

jargon.definition: A mechanism that lets each token weigh the relevance of other tokens.
jargon.why_it_matters: It replaces recurrence as the main way to mix information.

jargon.definition: Test information accidentally available during training or model selection.
jargon.why_it_matters: It makes benchmark scores look better than they are.

key_numbers.label: BLEU
key_numbers.quote: Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German task.

charts.title: BLEU on WMT 2014
charts.source_quote: The baseline reaches 26.0 BLEU, while our model achieves 28.4 BLEU.
charts.caption: Headline BLEU comparison.

limitations.limitation: Attention is quadratic in sequence length, which limits very long inputs.
The leakage estimate depends on the benchmark's split metadata.

comparison.takeaway: The papers address different problems, but both show that evaluation design changes the headline number.

topic_connections.connection: Leakage can inflate benchmark scores when test data appears in training.
topic_connections.quote: We find that 12% of test examples appear in the training split.
